summary: Assign the existing 101/2 livelihood example to new subsense 1b.
rationale: The poor man lacks sufficient means and hunts for subsistence; no new quotation is needed.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (Jan 3.7/88)

data.turoyo: Noše kkəṯwi w kəbʕi mu Xori, d samme ṭalabiyat l Awruppa. Ṭlobo d waroqe rasmi lašan təqḏ̣iyo d šuġlone w ḥatta gəworo. Ax xadamatani kulle məṭləbiwo mu Xori.
data.translation: People write and ask the Khori to make applications for them to Europe. Requests for official papers for carrying out business and even marrying. All these services used to be requested of the Khori.

rationale: New III Infinitiv box: təqḏ̣iyo d šuġlone is carrying out business in a purpose phrase. The active action nominal alone does not establish Detransitive morphology.

summary: New sense 1b: auskommen, genug zum Leben haben
rationale: Positive koqoḏ̣eno with family bread and surplus (47/9), negative livelihood qoḏ̣ewo (101/2, already cited), and positive qəḏenawo in employment (Bilgic /11) establish financial sufficiency independently of the translations.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum-wa (Bilgic Der Beruf eines Kesselverzinkers/11)

data.turoyo: Tamo qəḏenawo kayiso w bol-bol ste, yaʕni latwayna muḥtaǧ d əmmina d əṯena l Almanya ste."
data.translation: (Betreffs der) Arbeit kamen wir sehr gut aus, sehr gut sogar, so daß wir eigentlich nicht nach Deutschland ziehen brauchten.

rationale: Thin newly distinguished I livelihood Infectum-wa cell; positive customary earnings contrast with inherited negative 101/2.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum (47/9)

data.turoyo: Huleli mede mine, ṭowo yo. Luleli ste naqla ḥreto, škur mene d aloho, kali koqoḏ̣eno w konofəq u laḥmo dan naʕimayḏi w kozoyəd."
data.translation: Wenn er mir etwas davon gibt, so ist es gut; und wenn er mir nichts gibt, so komme ich - Gott sei gedankt! - immer noch aus, und das Brot für meine Familie kommt heraus und es bleibt noch übrig."

rationale: Clear positive livelihood context with family bread and surplus; first Infectum quotation for subsense 1b.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Ditin Hazar/5)

data.turoyo: ‘Mə‿kəbʕutu?’ Omar, ‘Kobaʕno ṗire’. Əmmi, ‘Hăma, a+tlaṯayna aḥwóṯena’. Omar, ‘Mən koqoḏe ab̥xu?’
data.translation: ‘What does Your Majesty want?’ He said, ‘I want a wife.’ ‘Well, the three of us are sisters.’ He said, ‘What do you do?’ (lit. ‘what passes with you’)

rationale: Better capacity context than isolated 96/114; plural b-participants and the edition's literal explanatory rendering.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (94/205)

data.turoyo: Aš šuġlone du ṭaʕno kulle bu ḥmoro koqoḏ̣ən.
data.translation: Das lasttragen geschieht durchweg auf dem Esel.

rationale: Unusual plural task subject and b-animal instrument; complements inherited singular spindle example, without a Detransitive label.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC NE Habirman Xatun/3)

data.turoyo: L Ăḷo maqḏele la+tre. Be mən hawi, l Ăḷo sәmle. L Ăḷo húlela k̇ačk̇e, maḥatla әšma Ḥabәrmán Xatun.
data.translation: God made it come to pass for the two. Whatever happened, God did it. God gave her a girl, she called her (lit. ‘put her name’) Lady Pomegranate Seed.

rationale: Unusual III accomplishment with l-marked God agent and l-beneficiaries, contextualised by the birth.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (69/530)

data.translation: Komm! Es ist ja nur eine Nacht, Gott wird sie schon vorübergehen lassen.

rationale: III causes a night to pass, contrasting I temporal subject; informative argument contrast.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (94/170)

data.turoyo: Yalənəz, u yawmo towe naxwaš, wayaxud towe kabisat, lo koməfqi u sawal lu ṭuro. Kobənne ṭarfe w ftile, komaqḏ̣ən hul foṯe du rabəʕ.
data.translation: Nur, wenn einmal ein Tag schlechtes Wetter ist, oder wenn es Länger anhaltenden Schneefall gibt, lassen sie das Vieh nicht auf den Berg hinaus, sondern geben ihm Baumblätter und Heuwickel zu fressen. So verbringen sie die Zeit bis zum Frühlingsanfang.

rationale: III time-spending without an overt time object, with endpoint hul foṯe du rabəʕ.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.23/4066)
rationale: Distinct subject sniquṯayḏan, with I kquḏyo and no agent. The unusual need-subject frame is worth preserving beyond routine full-cell filling.

summary: Remove an extra n in “my watch”
rationale: The cited corpus verse reads “maqḏ̣eli i nobayḏi” and earlier “di noba”. The entry adds an n after nob-, which is not a clitic-boundary or stress normalization.

summary: Remove an extra syllable in the word for “their weapons”
rationale: The supplied verse reads “mzabanne a slaḥaṯṯe”. The entry has slaḥat-aṯṯe, adding -at- before the ending. The proposed form retains the entry’s article boundary and matches the cited word.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
after: erledigen, verbringen, abmachen, beendigen, durchführen; Bedarf decken, mit etwas auskommen;
rationale: Add the meaning of covering needs/getting by on resources, already exemplified by 11/92 and the inherited maqḏ̣ina ape a=kmo=yawm-anək; retain the old meanings and numbering.

summary: I qaḏ̣i Preterit Intransitive marks completed intervals and settled states, not formal Detransitive morphology. Duration plus l-participant (65/140; Oṣman-Aġa /7; 95/230) leaves impersonal elapsed time versus a reanalysed spending pattern open.
I financial sufficiency is established across independent texts, including positive earnings and negative poverty. Distinguish this from general impersonal manage/be possible, which remains sense 1.
II mqaḏ̣eli at 31/33 and III maqḏ̣eli/maqḏ̣alle both spend time. Retain the inherited stem split rather than deriving assignment from German verbringen.
III completes a task, spends an interval, causes a night to pass, and covers a household's needs. Resource construction already exists in the entry, so its gloss is clarified rather than duplicated.
The inherited I gloss contains literal numbering text '1. ...; 2.' inside parsed sense 1. Preserve it; use 1b without creating or filling the unexplained empty 2.

Counts in the supplied entry are 7 I Preterit Intransitive examples, 5 I Infectum, and 5 III Preterit, including source notes. Reader claims of eleven independent examples are not supported by this parsed inventory.
MAC Interview 2/211 matches the untranslated Nisane 243 sentence already in III Preterit. Do not supply a translation against that inherited citation without confirming the edition concordance.
Jan English is machine translation [MT]. Neither its sufficed, served nor finished off automatically establishes a new stem or sense.
Round 1 already established I.1b financial sufficiency and clarified III.1 resource sufficiency. The Jan proposals are assessed against that revised state.

III spending takes explicit intervals: military service, summer, winter, nights, and life. Jan 2.10/2290 also has a completed journey. These do not require separate time, journey or military-service senses.

The purpose nominal təqḏ̣iyo d šuġlone is assigned provisionally to the III carrying-out meaning rather than the inherited II time-spending meaning. Arabic taqḍiya contact is possible; the t-prefix alone is not evidence for a Detransitive reading.

Jan 3.12/122 has qḏ̣ewole ʕal human communities after burning buildings and killing/wounding. It indicates destructive action against communal presence; it does not state that every person was killed. Stem and -wa/-le segmentation remain unresolved, so no stem-bound numbered sense is published.

The recurrent Aloho maqḏ̣əyole/maqḏəyole formula may express completion, outcome or requital in different contexts. Jan does not resolve the suffix question already raised in round 1; no reward gloss or new idiom is manufactured.
Plain ḏ and dotted ḏ̣ alternate in the supplied transcription. Source forms are retained exactly rather than harmonized to the glossary root spelling.
Does 95/7 haw qoḏ̣e contain a negator or an edition problem? Do not infer negative morphology solely from German 'er kam nicht aus'.
In 95/230 qaḏ̣ila, is -la a dative participant with elapsed duration, or an agent of a transitive I spending form? Compare the Oṣman-Aġa and personal-communication examples.
Does MAC Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/4 ʕam mark a person one cannot cope with, or the situation shared with him?
Confirm the possessor and syntax of m iḏe lo koqoḏ̣e yo in Talay 1/387, and the LB 387 concordance.
Check PrS 71/5 Gmaqḏ̣ena versus inherited prs 201/2 g-maqḏ̣eno and u maqriyono before changing citation or wording.
Confirm maqəḏyole in MAC Interview 2/247, la+tre in MAC Habirman Xatun/3, and the source meaning of Nisane 243.
What did the empty '2.' in the inherited I gloss introduce? Preserve current numbering until the source is recovered.

Parse qḏ̣ewole at Jan 3.12/122: I suffixing Preterit-wa, a reduced III form, or another construction? What explains -le with Tərkiya, contrasting earlier feminine agreement? Only then assign the destructive ʕal construction to a stem.
Does Jan 2.8/2031 qaḏ̣i šuġle express sufficient livelihood or simply settled business? It is provisional support for round-1 I.1b.
Confirm III versus II and borrowing status for təqḏ̣iyo at Jan 3.7/88; ordinary Infinitiv is a provisional semantic placement, not a claim about an unattested finite paradigm.
What is the force and segmentation of Aloho maqḏ̣əyole at Jan 2.4/526,900,924 and maqḏiyole at 2.29/4711: completion, retrospective thanks, or requital?
German typo: “wil” → “will”
rationale: German first-person singular is “ich will”. The supplied edition translation at 33/41 also has “will ich erzählen”.

summary: b- can introduce a capable participant (96/114; MAC /5), a tool (94/5,262), or an animal used to carry out work (94/204–205,218). The semantic role follows the task and participant, not the preposition alone.
A judicial sentence is completed before the prisoners leave; the legal object extends existing completion/time-spending rather than establishing a separate technical sense.
qaḏ̣i šuġle in a livelihood description provisionally supports round-1 sufficiency. Literal completed-business interpretation remains possible; no duplicate new sense is proposed.
sniquṯayḏan is the fulfilled need as subject, while person-centred livelihood is round-1 1b.
